doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: The 1950s guitar club and first session with strings
summary: Studio call order led by Tony Mottola; Pallo substitutes on a Tony Hatch session for Petula Clark with strings and a borrowed twelve-string.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: The guitar really became very important in pop music.
Just about good timing for you, don’t you think?

That’s right, yes. And in the fifties is when they had like a guitar club where Tony Mottola was number one, Bucky was involved on that, Al Caiola and so many of them, Barry Galbraith, and whenever they had recording sessions that’s the way it would go. Tony would be the first one called out and if he couldn’t make it then it would be the next one, I forgot who was second but say Al Caiola or somebody, then Bucky and on down the line. And I got on a few of those, which was great because I was maybe the thirtieth down the line. There were so many. And I would have to replace like with Tony Hatch with —

Petula Clark. Okay. I had to do a rhythm section thing on that with Tony Hatch and Barry Galbraith was supposed to do it and then he called me and then I did it. So that was, and that was my first experience doing a recording session with strings. Oh —
Heaven. And they were all, can I tell you about this?

The string section is in front of me in the studio and the violins, the cellos, and so on, facing me. And here I am with my music stand facing them. Next to me was another guitarist, I can’t think of who was on that session, and I was playing a twelve string. I borrowed Les’ twelve string guitar for that because I didn’t have one. And I’m looking at the music, I’m turning the pages, all the string section, they’re all reading the New York Times, reading the newspapers, waiting until you hear Tony Hatch come in and say, “Okay one, two, three,” and they just put down the newspaper and they go [scats] and they read the score and they’re reading notes like all the way down and here I am looking at the chart for a good ten minutes before they started the session. What readers they are.
